title: Sunday Special: The 100 Best Books of the Century (So Far)

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我曾在凌晨4点半给总统打电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 探索太空的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于助您了解世界，充实每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享优惠，请访问 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: Hi everyone.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: It's Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We're taking a break from our usual weekend routine to bring you something special today.
sentences.zh: 我们今天暂停常规的周末节目，为大家带来一些特别内容。

sentences.en: It's summer.
sentences.zh: 夏天到了。

sentences.en: It's beach reading time.
sentences.zh: 这是海滩阅读的好时光。

sentences.en: Maybe you need a book to take a break from the news.
sentences.zh: 也许你需要一本书来远离新闻，放松一下。

sentences.en: Anyway, our wonderful colleagues at the New York Times Book Review recently compiled a list of the 100 best books of the 21st century so far.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们在《纽约时报书评》的优秀同事最近整理了一份“21世纪至今100本最佳图书”书单。

sentences.en: To be clear, this is not a list of bestsellers.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，这并非一份畅销书榜单。

sentences.en: Or just literary award winners.
sentences.zh: 也不是单纯的文学奖获奖名单。

sentences.en: I mean, there's some of those.
sentences.zh: 我是说，里面确实包含了一些。

sentences.en: But to make their list, they surveyed more than 500 novelists, poets, critics, editors, and readers.
sentences.zh: 但为了完成这份书单，他们调查了超过500位小说家、诗人、评论家、编辑和读者。

sentences.en: It's a very cool project.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常酷的项目。

sentences.en: And it's a super interesting liSt.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一份超级有趣的书单。

sentences.en: It's gotten a huge response.
sentences.zh: 它获得了巨大的反响。

sentences.en: And so today, we're sending you the episode of their podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以今天，我们将为你播放他们播客中的一期节目。

sentences.en: It's an episode about this list and what's on it.
sentences.zh: 这是一期关于这份书单及其入选作品的节目。

sentences.en: You should also know that beyond this episode, the New York Times Book Review's podcast comes out regularly.
sentences.zh: 你还应该知道，除了这期节目，《纽约时报书评》的播客会定期更新。

sentences.en: They have fascinating conversations all the time, including with some of the phenomenal writers on this recent liSt.
sentences.zh: 他们经常进行精彩的对话，包括与这份近期书单中一些杰出作家的交流。

sentences.en: So sign up for their show wherever you listen to us.
sentences.zh: 所以，请在你收听我们节目的平台上订阅他们的节目。

sentences.en: Okay, here they are.
sentences.zh: 好了，接下来请听他们的节目。

sentences.en: I'm Gilbert Cruz, editor of the New York Times Book Review, and this is the Book Review PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔伯特·克鲁兹，《纽约时报书评》编辑，这是《书评播客》。

sentences.en: On this week's episode, I'm very excited to finally talk about a project that we've been working on for much of 2024, and which is finally out there in the world.
sentences.zh: 在本周的节目中，我非常激动地终于要谈谈我们从2024年大部分时间就开始筹备，且终于面世的一个项目。

sentences.en: 100 best books of the 21st century so far.
sentences.zh: “21世纪至今100本最佳图书”。

sentences.en: If you're listening to this show, if you're listening to a podcast about books, I have to think you've already seen part or all of it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在听这个节目，如果你在听一个关于书的播客，我想你一定已经看过其中的部分或全部内容了。

sentences.en: Joining me this week are three editors who have been deep in the weeds with me on this since January.
sentences.zh: 本周加入我的是三位编辑，他们从一月份起就和我一起深入钻研这个项目。

sentences.en: Tina Jordan, hello.
sentences.zh: 蒂娜·乔丹，你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Jew Monica T.
sentences.zh: 舒马纳·T。

sentences.en: Welcome back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回来。

sentences.en: Hi, Gilbert.
sentences.zh: 你好，吉尔伯特。

sentences.en: And Scott Heller.
sentences.zh: 还有斯科特·海勒。

sentences.en: This is your first time on the show.
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次上节目。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I'm a listener now.
sentences.zh: 我现在也是个听众了。

sentences.en: I'm excited to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I'm excited to have all of you on.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你们都能来。

sentences.en: So I'm hoping we can have a free-flowing discussion about this effort, about some of the books on the list, books that didn't make the liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望我们能就这项工作、书单上的一些书，以及那些没能入选的书，进行一场畅所欲言的讨论。

sentences.en: There's a lot to dig into here.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多值得挖掘的内容。

sentences.en: And I want to start by asking someone else who's not me, Tina, why did we do this?
sentences.zh: 我想先问问除了我之外的其他人，蒂娜，我们为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Why did we do this?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要这么做？

sentences.en: Because we looked around and we, it was almost the quarter century mark.
sentences.zh: 因为我们环顾四周，发现这几乎到了四分之一个世纪的节点。

sentences.en: We're book nerds who like to categorize and make lists.
sentences.zh: 我们这些书呆子喜欢分类和制作榜单。

sentences.en: And we thought, what are the best books of the 21st century so far?
sentences.zh: 于是我们想，21世纪至今最好的书是什么？

sentences.en: And we started to argue about it.
sentences.zh: 我们开始为此争论。

sentences.en: We started to talk ourselves about the things we'd read since January 1st, 2000 that we loved.
sentences.zh: 我们开始谈论自2000年1月1日以来我们读过并喜爱的作品。

sentences.en: And then we thought, hey, maybe there's something here, but let's put this out to a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 然后我们想，嘿，也许这事儿有搞头，但让我们把它推向更多人。

sentences.en: Because normally we would have just done this in-house.
sentences.zh: 因为通常我们只会内部完成。

sentences.en: We would have polled the editors, polled the critics, our wonderful critics, and that would have been it.
sentences.zh: 我们会调查编辑们、评论家们，我们优秀的评论家们，然后就结束了。

sentences.en: But this seemed like an opportunity to do something bigger.
sentences.zh: 但这似乎是一个做点大事的机会。

sentences.en: Given that we ask all these writers all the time to write for us, to review books, to appear in our pages, we figured we could actually use their voices towards something massive.
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们一直邀请这些作家为我们撰稿、评论书籍、在我们的版面上亮相，我们想我们可以利用他们的声音来完成一件宏大的事情。

sentences.en: And this thing is massive.
sentences.zh: 而这件事确实很宏大。

sentences.en: Scott, as someone who's still relatively new to the desk, as new as I am, who've only been here about two years,
sentences.zh: 斯科特，作为刚加入编辑部不久的人，和我一样，只在这里待了大约两年，

sentences.en: is what was the most surprising thing to you about this effort, this project?
sentences.zh: 对于这项工作、这个项目，最让你惊讶的是什么？

sentences.en: What ended up being most surprising, actually, was how many people were willing to share their ballots.
sentences.zh: 最令人惊讶的其实是，有多少人愿意分享他们的投票名单。

sentences.en: We bent over backwards to let people know this was anonymous.
sentences.zh: 我们竭尽全力让大家知道这是匿名的。

sentences.en: And don't worry, we're not going to reveal who you pick, who you left off.
sentences.zh: 别担心，我们不会透露你选了谁，或者漏掉了谁。

sentences.en: And yet so many people were willing to come forward with what they selected.
sentences.zh: 然而，还是有那么多人愿意公开他们的选择。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of the best things about it, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为这是它最棒的地方之一。

sentences.en: The aggregated list is wonderful and there's plenty to argue about.
sentences.zh: 汇总后的书单很棒，有很多值得争论的地方。

sentences.en: But when you go get in and dig into what Stephen King put on his list, in fact, he put himself on his list, which I think people have gotten a kick out of,
sentences.zh: 但当你深入了解斯蒂芬·金在他的名单上写了什么时——事实上，他把自己也写进了名单，我想大家对此感到很有趣——

sentences.en: but many others came forward.
sentences.zh: 但还有许多其他人也站了出来。

sentences.en: And I think that makes for sort of wonderful reading in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 我认为这本身就构成了一种美妙的阅读体验。

sentences.en: And also, you get to see a lot of quirky choices that maybe many people didn't vote for, but that individuals are passionate about.
sentences.zh: 而且，你还能看到许多独特的选择，也许很多人没投它们，但个人却对它们充满热情。

sentences.en: And I really enjoyed that.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: Scott, I think you're right.
sentences.zh: 斯科特，我想你是对的。

sentences.en: I think seeing some of the ballots possibly is more entertaining to some of our readers than seeing the list itself.
sentences.zh: 我认为对我们的一些读者来说，看一些投票名单可能比看书单本身更有趣。

sentences.en: I have to say, in our earliest discussions about this project, one of the things that was an inspiration, certainly for me, was the Sight & Sound liSt.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，在我们关于这个项目的早期讨论中，对我而言，灵感来源之一无疑是《视与听》杂志的榜单。

sentences.en: For those of you who don't know, Sight & Sound is a British film journal.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的人，介绍一下，《视与听》是一本英国电影杂志。

sentences.en: And ever since 1952 or 1962, every 10 years, they've taken a poll of critics, and then it turned into a poll of critics and film directors,
sentences.zh: 自1952年或1962年以来，每隔10年，他们都会进行一次评论家投票，后来演变成评论家和电影导演的联合投票，

sentences.en: and they asked them to put their top films of all time.
sentences.zh: 他们要求他们列出自己心目中史上最伟大的电影。

sentences.en: And every 10 years, it's a big deal when this list runs, particularly over the past couple decades, because not only do they run the list,
sentences.zh: 每隔10年，这份榜单发布时都是一件大事，尤其是在过去几十年里，因为他们不仅发布榜单，

sentences.en: but they run the ballots of the most famous critics and the most famous directors.
sentences.zh: 还发布了最著名评论家和导演的投票名单。

sentences.en: You can see what Guillermo del Toro and Barry Jenkins, and I don't know if Steven Spielberg participated, but you can imagine all the people whose lists are on there
sentences.zh: 你可以看到吉尔莫·德尔·托罗和巴里·詹金斯选了什么，我不知道史蒂文·斯皮尔伯格是否参与了，但你可以想象所有那些出现在名单上的人，

sentences.en: and just get a real sense of their taste.
sentences.zh: 从而真正了解他们的品味。

sentences.en: And then the other thing that is interesting about this list is that it changes over time.
sentences.zh: 关于这份榜单，另一件有趣的事情是它会随着时间而改变。

sentences.en: So Citizen Kane was the top movie for many decades, and then Vertigo was the top movie, and now there's a French movie,
sentences.zh: 所以《公民凯恩》曾占据榜首几十年，然后是《迷魂记》，现在有一部法国电影，

sentences.en: Jean Dielman, other French words I cannot pronounce, that is the top movie.
sentences.zh: 《让娜·迪尔曼》，还有其他我念不出来的法语词，成了榜首电影。

sentences.en: I'm not saying we're going to do this every 10 years, but it certainly is an inspiration to try to capture a moment in time.
sentences.zh: 我不是说我们要每10年做一次，但这确实是捕捉特定时刻的灵感来源。

sentences.en: And whatever else you want to say about this list, it is a snapshot of this moment in time.
sentences.zh: 无论你对这份书单有何评价，它都是这个时刻的快照。

sentences.en: There are probably books on here.
sentences.zh: 榜单上可能有一些书，

sentences.en: If you took this poll at the end of this year, it would not be on here.
sentences.zh: 如果你在今年年底进行这项调查，它就不会出现在上面了。

sentences.en: If you had taken it earlier, they would not be on here.
sentences.zh: 如果你早点进行调查，它们也不会出现在上面。

sentences.en: This is what people in the spring of 2024 that we polled thought were the 100 best books.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在2024年春季调查的人们心目中100本最佳图书。

sentences.en: So let's talk about some of these books.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来谈谈其中一些书。

sentences.en: I'd love to start with our number one book,
sentences.zh: 我想从我们的第一名开始，

sentences.en: which, I don't know, were people surprised?
sentences.zh: 我不知道，大家感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: Was anyone in this room at least surprised that My Brilliant Friend by Elena Ferrante was, according to our 503 respondents, the number one book of the 21st century?
sentences.zh: 在这个房间里，有没有人对埃琳娜·费兰特的《我的天才女友》根据我们503位受访者的意见成为21世纪第一名感到惊讶？

sentences.en: I was surprised.
sentences.zh: 我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But maybe I shouldn't have been because, as a reminder to our listeners,
sentences.zh: 但也许我不该感到惊讶，因为提醒一下我们的听众，

sentences.en: we asked our respondents to choose what they thought were the 10 best books of the century so far.
sentences.zh: 我们要求受访者选出他们心目中本世纪至今最好的10本书。

sentences.en: But we didn't define best for them.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有为他们定义什么是“最好”。

sentences.en: And people clearly defined it in different ways.
sentences.zh: 人们显然以不同的方式定义了它。

sentences.en: They defined it as the book they loved that they pass along to people.
sentences.zh: 他们将其定义为他们喜爱并会推荐给别人的书。

sentences.en: They defined it as the books they thought would still be around generations from now.
sentences.zh: 他们将其定义为他们认为几代人之后依然会流传的书。

sentences.en: But it really seems to me that a lot of the people who took our poll were just, like, voting for the books that had struck them, right?
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，很多参与调查的人只是在投票给那些打动他们的书，对吧？

sentences.en: The books they could not get out of their heads.
sentences.zh: 那些他们无法忘怀的书。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And I think we're all going to touch on what books fell into our own personal categories of books we couldn't get out of our head.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都会谈谈哪些书属于我们个人心目中无法忘怀的类别。

sentences.en: But talk a little bit more about Ferrante.
sentences.zh: 但再多谈谈费兰特吧。

sentences.en: Thankfully, luckily, we have a Ferrante expert on here.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，幸运的是，我们这里有一位费兰特专家。

sentences.en: Apparently, there's several Ferrante experts on the desk, but we have one who is in studio, who wrote a wonderful article that published in conjunction
sentences.zh: 显然，编辑部里有几位费兰特专家，但我们有一位在演播室里，她写了一篇精彩的文章，与这个项目同时发布，

sentences.en: with this project, looking at all the theories about who Elena Ferrante is.
sentences.zh: 探讨了关于埃琳娜·费兰特真实身份的所有理论。

sentences.en: Elena Ferrante is an author who uses an alias.
sentences.zh: 埃琳娜·费兰特是一位使用化名的作家。

sentences.en: We don't really know who the author is.
sentences.zh: 我们并不真正知道作者是谁。

sentences.en: There are theories and suspicions.
sentences.zh: 有一些理论和猜测。

sentences.en: But first, Shumana, I'd love for you to talk about just the book and maybe the Neapolitan
sentences.zh: 但首先，舒马纳，我想请你谈谈这本书，或许还有整个“那不勒斯四部曲”。

sentences.en: Quartet as a whole.
sentences.zh: 其中两本出现在了这份书单上。

sentences.en: Two of them appeared on this liSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，成为一个我们甚至不知道是谁的人的专家，这本身就带有一种讽刺意味。

sentences.en: There is, of course, some irony of being an expert on somebody that we don't even know who it is.
sentences.zh: 但我会自豪地接受这一点。

sentences.en: But I will lean into that with pride.
sentences.zh: 所以，蒂娜，我其实同意你的看法，看到《我的天才女友》排在第一位我也很惊讶。

sentences.en: So, Tina, I actually agree with you that I was surprised to see My Brilliant Friend firSt.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为它是几件事的良好体现。

sentences.en: I do think it's a nice representation of a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 显然，整个四部曲深深触动了人们。

sentences.en: Obviously, this whole quartet touched people really deeply.
sentences.zh: 但我也认为，我们大家都还没从“费兰特热”中完全走出来。

sentences.en: But also, I think we're all still coming out of Ferrante fever.
sentences.zh: 你还记得那些每个人都在读这些书的岁月吗？

sentences.en: Do you remember those years where everybody was reading these books?
sentences.zh: 就像当她有新书出版，或者HBO改编剧播出时，那真是一场盛事。

sentences.en: Like, it was an actual event when she had a new book coming out when the HBO adaptations were on.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢这个榜首选择，它代表了看待“最好”真正含义的几种不同方式。

sentences.en: So I liked that this top pick represents a couple different ways of looking at what best really means.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没被“费兰特热”感染，《我的天才女友》是四部曲系列中的第一本，现在被称为“那不勒斯四部曲”。

sentences.en: In case you are one of the people who has not been infected with Ferrante fever, My Brilliant
sentences.zh: 它讲述了两个在那不勒斯长大的女孩之间终身的友谊。

sentences.en: Friend is the first in a series of four books that is now known as the Neapolitan Quartet.
sentences.zh: 她们很贫穷。

sentences.en: It follows a lifelong friendship between two girls who are growing up in Naples.
sentences.zh: 她们都极其聪明。

sentences.en: They're poor.
sentences.zh: 她们从少女时代起就表现出超乎寻常的智慧，并且超乎寻常地依恋彼此。

sentences.en: They're both fiercely intelligent.
sentences.zh: 她们是彼此的镜像。

sentences.en: They're both preternaturally smart and preternaturally attached to each other from the time that they're young girls.
sentences.zh: 这是一种充满张力的关系。

sentences.en: They are doubles of one another.
sentences.zh: 有嫉妒。

sentences.en: And it's a very charged relationship.
sentences.zh: 有竞争。

sentences.en: There's jealousy.
sentences.zh: 但它也建立在一种只有在你那个年纪，与那样一个朋友建立联系时，才能真正培养出的爱之上。

sentences.en: There's rivalry.
sentences.zh: 我想我几乎是在它刚出英文版时就读了。

sentences.en: But it's also built on a type of love that you only, I think, can really foster when you're at that age and you attach on a friend like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我追踪了所有这些小说出版的过程。
